notes: The source PDF itself prints no diocese name anywhere -- only the generic page-wide header '2026 Diocesan Prayer Cycle', with no logo, letterhead, or footer text naming the diocese. `diocese` is instead taken from the diocese's own website's self-identification: 'The Episcopal Diocese of Wyoming' (the page title at episcopalwy.org, which hosts this PDF); that site's own footer copyright line reads 'Episcopal Diocese of Wyoming', without 'The'.

Full calendar-year weekly cycle, all 52 Sundays, January 4 - December 27, 2026, transcribed from a single-page, two-column table (January-June printed in a left column, July-December in a right column, side by side on one page). Because January 1, 2026 falls on a Thursday, every Sunday of the year falls within this January 4 - December 27 span already, with no week left over at either end -- there is no year-boundary gap or overlap of the kind this corpus's other partial-year sources have had to disclose-and-exclude or split across files.

Given the two-column layout's known interleaving risk for this corpus, the page was rendered to a 300dpi image and read visually (in four overlapping strips) rather than trusted from a linearized text extraction alone; 'pdftotext -layout''s own row-by-row output was then compared line by line against the rendered image and found to match throughout.
Curly apostrophes (’) are used throughout, matching the source PDF's own typography exactly, per this corpus's standing rule against silently normalizing a source's own printed text.

Five dates pair two distinct named congregations on one printed line, joined by a slash ('X/Y'), rather than the source's own multi-column congregation layout used elsewhere in this corpus (e.g. Southern Ohio) -- each such line is transcribed here as two separate `parish` subjects sharing the one date, in the order printed, rather than as one combined name, since each side names an organizationally distinct congregation:

- April 19: 'St. Matthew's Cathedral, Laramie/St. Alban's Chapel' -- the second congregation, 'St. Alban's Chapel', is given no comma-separated place of its own in the source; `place` 'Laramie' is inferred here from its pairing with St. Matthew's Cathedral (itself in Laramie), disclosed on that subject via its own `note`.

- May 17: 'St. Alban's, Worland/St. Christopher's Chapel' -- 'St. Christopher's Chapel' likewise has no place of its own printed; `place` 'Worland' is inferred from the pairing, disclosed via that subject's own `note`. This is a distinct congregation from 'St. Christopher's, Cheyenne' printed later at August 16 -- same patron saint, two different places.
- July 12: 'Christ Church, Cody/Wayfarers Chapel' -- 'Wayfarers Chapel' has no place of its own printed; `place` 'Cody' is inferred from the pairing, disclosed via that subject's own `note`.

- July 19: 'St. John's, Jackson/Chapel of the Transfiguration' -- 'Chapel of the Transfiguration' has no place of its own printed; `place` 'Jackson' is inferred from the pairing, disclosed via that subject's own `note`. The real chapel building (in Grand Teton National Park) is more precisely located in Moose, Wyoming, not Jackson itself, but the source does not print a separate place for it, so 'Jackson' (from the pairing) is used rather than substituting outside knowledge the source itself does not give.

- August 9: 'St. Andrew's, Atlantic City/Oregon Trail Memorial, Eden' -- included here for contrast: both halves of this slash pairing DO carry their own source-given place ('Atlantic City' and 'Eden'), so no place was inferred for either subject.

Three further dates pair two diocesan bodies with a slash rather than two congregations: January 11 'Standing Committee/COM', June 14 'Diocesan Council/Foundation Board', and December 27 'Diocesan Staff/TAC' -- each transcribed as two separate `category` subjects sharing the one date. 'COM' and 'TAC' are kept exactly as printed, undecoded abbreviations (plausibly 'Commission on Ministry' and a diocesan committee, respectively) -- not expanded or guessed at, per this corpus's rule against silently altering a source's own text.

August 2's 'Our Partner Dioceses - Leicester (U.K), Kiteto and Mt. Kilimanjaro (Tanzania), Trichy-Tanjore (India)' is transcribed as a single `category` subject with this entire phrase as its `name`, rather than split into three subjects, because the source phrases it as one continuous sentence (unlike the short slash-joined pairs above). The source's own '(U.K)' (missing the second period one would expect in 'U.K.') is preserved exactly as printed.

Apostrophe/spelling inconsistencies are preserved verbatim, not corrected: 'All Soul's, Kaycee' (Feb 1) uses a singular possessive, where 'All Souls'' (plural possessive) would be the conventional styling many Episcopal congregations of that name use; 'All Saints, Torrington' (Dec 6) carries no apostrophe at all, unlike 'All Saints', Wheatland' (Jun 21) earlier in the very same document; and 'St Hubert's, Bondurant' (Dec 13) omits the period after 'St' that the source otherwise uses consistently everywhere else (e.g. 'St. Andrew's') -- the same kind of preserved period-omission typo as this corpus's own Southern Ohio precedent file's 'St Patrick's'.

The source's own table prints a stray blank underscored line immediately after the 'August 2026' column heading (a trailing table-cell border, not text) -- it carries no content and has no corresponding entry in this file.
No liturgical annotations (e.g. 'Advent', 'Proper 15') are printed anywhere in this source -- `liturgicalNote` is null on every entry.
